Tests of a model's parameters

Source: R/test_parameter.R
test_parameter.Rd

These generics test hypotheses about the parameters of a fitted model:

  • test_parameter() asks whether one or more parameters have the values that a hypothesis gives them.

  • test_time() asks whether parameters are constant over time.

Each has a method for a netreg, from estimate_mrqap(). {infernet} holds the generics so that other packages can register methods for their own models on them.

Usage

test_parameter(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
test_parameter(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netreg'
test_parameter(x, terms, value = 0, ..., times = 1000, control = list())

test_time(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
test_time(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netreg'
test_time(x, terms = NULL, ..., times = 1000, control = list())

Arguments

x

A fitted model, such as a netreg from estimate_mrqap().

...

Arguments for a method. Not used by the methods for a netreg.

terms

The names of the coefficients to test, as the model prints them, such as "ego_Age". A name that is not a coefficient selects every coefficient that starts with it and an underscore, so "ego_Grp" selects the levels "ego_Grp_b" and "ego_Grp_c". For test_time(), NULL tests every coefficient but the intercept.

value

The value of the coefficients under the hypothesis: one number for all of them, or one for each.

times

The number of permutations.

control

A list of controls, or the result of control_mrqap(). The tests read seed, strategy, ncores, and groups, and the controls set with control_mrqap(..., persist = TRUE) where these are not named.

Value

For a netreg, a network_test, with the statistic, the permutation distribution, and the p-value as pgteobs. It also holds the tested coefficients as terms, the tested values as value, and the number of permutations left out because the model did not converge on them as failed.

Details

For a netreg, both tests compare a model in which the tested coefficients are free with one in which they are fixed. The statistic is the deviance that freeing them removes: the residual sum of squares of a gaussian model, and the deviance of a binomial or poisson one. The p-value comes from a joint double semi-partialling (Dekker, Krackhardt and Snijders 2007). Each tested predictor is residualised on the untested ones, one permutation of the nodes is applied to all the residuals together, and the model is fitted again. The permutations exchange only nodes whose unobserved cells match, as estimate_mrqap() does, so every permutation uses the dyads of the observed model. The p-value is $$p = \frac{1 + \#\{s_{perm} \geq s_{obs}\}}{1 + k}$$ where \(k\) is the number of permutations that the model could be fitted to.

With one tested coefficient, this is the test that estimate_mrqap() gives that coefficient under permute = "predictor", with the deviance in place of the t-statistic. Its value is that it can test several coefficients together, such as the levels of a categorical attribute, and test a value other than 0.

test_parameter() tests that the coefficients of terms equal value. In a gaussian model it subtracts value times each predictor from the outcome, and tests that the coefficients of the result are 0. In a binomial or poisson model, value must be 0, since a value there would be an offset, and an offset under permutation has no clear meaning.

test_time() tests that each coefficient of terms is the same in every fitted wave of a panel. It adds an interaction of each tested predictor with each fitted wave after the first, and an intercept for each such wave, and tests that the interactions are all 0. The intercepts for the waves are not tested, since the density of a network often changes from wave to wave. One permutation relabels the nodes in the same way in every wave.

Network regressions

Both methods read the dyads that the model kept, so they do not need the network again. They cannot yet test a model of a cognitive social structure, a model with random intercepts, or a model with fixed effects that is not gaussian. A model fitted with groups needs the same groups in control. test_time() needs a panel, a longitudinal network that estimate_mrqap() fits wave by wave. A list of networks is not a panel, since nothing says that its networks are in time order.

Other packages

{RSiena} and {goldfish} export test_parameter() and test_time() generics with the same signature, for their own fitted models. If more than one of these packages is attached, the one attached last masks the others. Call infernet::test_parameter(), RSiena::test_parameter(), or goldfish::test_parameter() to choose.

References

Dekker, David, David Krackhardt, and Tom A. B. Snijders. 2007. "Sensitivity of MRQAP Tests to Collinearity and Autocorrelation Conditions." Psychometrika 72(4): 563-581. doi:10.1007/s11336-007-9016-1

See also

Other models: control_mrqap(), diagnose_confusion(), other_results, play_diffusions(), print.netreg_lm(), regression, specify, specify_terms, terms_mrqap, test_fit, test_measures

Examples

fit <- estimate_mrqap(. ~ ego(Grp) + alter(Age), ison_adolescents |>
  mutate_nodes(Grp = rep(c("a", "b", "c"), length.out = 8),
               Age = 12:19), times = 50)
# Do the groups differ, taking both levels together?
test_parameter(fit, "ego_Grp", times = 100, control = list(seed = 1))
#> # Parameter test of ego_Grp_b, ego_Grp_c = 0, 0 in a logistic MRQAP of ties
#> 
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   statistic null.mean null.sd p.lower p.upper signif   
#>       <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>   <chr>   <noquote>
#> 1      1.14      2.53    2.21 0.327   0.683            
#> 
#> # Null: 100 permutations of the tested predictors, by double semi-partialling.
#> # The p-value is p.upper: only a larger statistic counts against the null.
#> # Controls: seed = 1
